Raised from P3 and moved up 30: it is the stated prerequisite for #25573 (P2) and #36193, so it cannot sit below them.
Raised from P3 and moved up 22: same consequence as the g++13 bump (#36042, P2) — a dated toolchain transition enabling the C++23 baseline.
Raised from P3 for consistency with the other minimum-toolchain bumps it is part of (#36036/#36042).
Placed 7 below its score position: the decision matters but cannot land before the compiler-minimum bumps (#36042/#36036) it sits on.
Raised from P3: removes a recurring dependency burden across depends, Guix, vcpkg and platform workarounds — the textbook P2 'significant recurring burden'.

Moved up: build-host path leakage into shipped binaries touches release hygiene, though nothing is currently broken.

Placed 9 below its score position: overlaps #28690's check-deps changes and fixes only internal check accuracy.

inconsistencies: #35855 and #36233 both bump the Guix time-machine and both close #36232 (native RISC-V builds). Review #35855 first as the broader toolchain refresh; #36233 only matters if #35855 stalls.
#36036 already bumps Xcode CLT to 26.3, which is all #36287 does. Either review #36287 first as the narrow prerequisite and rebase #36036 on it, or close one.
Toolchain chain, order matters: #36042 (g++ 13) and #36036/#36287 (Clang 19 / Xcode 26.3) are prerequisites for #36033 (C++23), which in turn unblocks #34979.
Guix chain: #36272 (toolchain split) must merge before #25573 (static-pie) and #36193 (--disable-wchar_t); both stacked PRs cite it.

#36275 is an extracted prerequisite for #36167 (-Wunused); review it first. #35911 (-Wmissing-noreturn) is the same class of warning enablement and several of these depend on subtree updates upstream.
#36235 and #36252 both modify the IWYU CI job; #36235 (fail on compiler errors) should go first, since #36252 (skip subtrees) changes what that job compiles.
#28690 adds dependency rules to check-deps.sh while #35167 rewrites check-deps.sh in Python; they collide and should be sequenced, with the library-boundary design question in #28690 settled first.
#36269 is stacked on #36082; the Guix CI workflow must land first.
#19460 depends on the multiprocess branch (#10102/#29409) and is the base of #19461 — its build content alone is minimal.
#35197 and #36193 are both release-binary size reductions of comparable value and are banded together.
result.notes: Bands were spread deliberately: one P1 (release-verification security), a P2 tier covering release-integrity CI, Guix/toolchain transitions and supported-platform build breakage, a large P3 tier of CI-reliability and contributor-friction work, and P4 for pure logging/formatting/warning cosmetics. Several P3 rankings were reshuffled so that CI jobs that silently hide failures (#36235, #36024) and measured CI speedups (#36121) sit above deferrable convenience and size-reduction work.
